label: Figure 30.2: The world market for cocoa
alt: Demand-and-supply diagram for the world cocoa market showing price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis, with a steep demand curve and three steep supply curves (S1, S2, S3) illustrating how small shifts in supply cause large price swings.
caption: Both demand D and supply S for cocoa are drawn steep (price-inelastic), typical of an agricultural commodity. Starting from S<sub>1</sub> at P<sub>1</sub> = $1,400 and Q<sub>1</sub> = 20 million tonnes, a bumper harvest shifts supply right to S<sub>2</sub>, and price falls sharply to P<sub>2</sub> = $1,280 for only a small rise to Q<sub>2</sub> = 22 million tonnes; a poor harvest shifts supply left to S<sub>3</sub>, and price jumps to P<sub>3</sub> = $1,520 as quantity falls only to Q<sub>3</sub> = 18 million tonnes. Because both curves are inelastic, small supply shocks cause disproportionately large price swings – a key source of instability for commodity-dependent economies.
